summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (94/442)

data.turoyo: U ḥa mənne, d qosəm, u madilono gdomalle: “Ḥat aʕlayye!” Edi hiye ste gmaḥət aʕlayye bi šutke.
data.translation: wenn einer richtig rät, so sagt der Beschreiber des Vogels zu ihm: "Hau sie!" Dann Haut er sie mit dem Wollgurt.

rationale: First Part act. box: substantivized participant in the ongoing description game, not the dll 2 town announcer.

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (94/444)

data.turoyo: Hawxa bu šəklano məqdar d ḥamməš daqayəq. Bəṯr u madilono gqore, gdomər: “Ǧaya!” Yaʕni sʕore ne. Disa gmaḥət aʕlayye.
data.translation: So geht es etwa fünfminnten lang, dann ruft der Beschreiber auf Kurdisch: "Es ist Gerste!" Dann Haut er sie wieder.

rationale: New Part act. box: same describing role controls calling out, confirming the participant reading.

summary: New idiom: lebo madəl l- 'jmdm. eine Ahnung eingeben'

data.headword: lebo madəl l- 'jmdm. eine Ahnung eingeben'
data.translation: <...> Aber es war, als ob mein Herz mir eine Ahnung eingäbe.

rationale: Required lookup searches lebi and madil find this existing dyl example but no idiom heading for the intuition construction. Heart as source and co-referential recipient specify the collocation; retain the edition's hedging.

summary: III combines recipient l-suffixes with ʕal-marked indicated targets, or zero-marked information objects. At 11/109 the overt l-marked angel is the sender/agent, not the recipient.
The related entry dll 2 has mdalele/mdaləl and the town-announcer noun dalolo. Lookup does not warrant moving directional showing forms out of dyl.
Direction-giving and describing by signs fit the existing gloss. madilono is an action participant in the bird game, even though substantivized; it does not establish a new numbered sense.
Apparent contraction/assimilation yields Madənnanxu and expanded madəllalle. Preserve surface spelling; the exact morphological segmentation is not silently normalized.
The heart-intuition idiom is attested once, in an already published example, with xəd 'as if'. No stronger assertion of premonition is introduced.

Jan 1.8/287 madiwolən supplies directional showing with a recipient suffix and quoted road information. The compressed past form cannot by itself justify a new Preterit-wa box against already attested Infectum-wa.
Jan 2.35/5625 has kmadilo lu qšoʕayḏan, not an overt first-person plural object on the verb. The machine lead us towards translation must not establish causation or a new valency frame.
All three occurrences fit existing III.1. After round 1 the relevant Infectum cell has five examples; no Jan example improves the coverage enough to add one. No new idiom or sense is established.
Resolve kmadile at PrS 18/48 before classifying it as Infectum or ko-Preterit; verify reciprocal agreement.
Confirm Madənnanxu as a contraction of madəl-no-lxu.
What are ak̇+k̇elik̇at du+bayto at MAC NE Keze/25: household items, arrangements, or literal moments? Do not derive a new sense from the free translation.
Confirm the equivalence of modern PrS 64/52 and inherited prs 181/6 before changing any citation; their sentence is identical.
Is madiwolən at Jan 1.8/287 Preterit-wa, Infectum-wa or another contracted sequence? Supply segmentation and agent/recipient identification.
Confirm indication rather than causal leading in kmadilo lu qšoʕayḏan (Jan 2.35/5625); review the machine translation before quoting it.
Correct the article in “eine lange Weile”
rationale: Weile is feminine; the duration phrase requires eine lange Weile. The supplied edition translation repeats the same grammatical slip, so this is a German correction, not a claim of disagreement with the corpus.

summary: Inanimate sources include a marker stone and a person's appearance/bearing. They indicate information under the existing gloss; no new sense is required.
A situation and a preceding assertion can indicate an outcome/proposition. This continues the inanimate-source pattern documented in round 1, without a causal lead-to sense.
